meanings.note: Land along the edge of water. Common masculine noun meaning 'shore, bank' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They will sit quietly on the shore.
They walked along the lake shore.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor

meanings.note: Ordinal number. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('second').

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'sofa, couch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is sitting on the sofa.
I will reach the sofa myself.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: A person's own room at work. From French 'cabinet' (private study or office).

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, я сейчас в кабинете у мэра.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, I'm in the mayor's office right now.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'on the ship' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас на корабле в океане генераторы отказали.
examples.trans: On our ship in the ocean all the generators failed.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть корабль.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always on the ship.

meanings.note: Short for может быть. Core Russian part meaning 'maybe, perhaps' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Surprise, fright or pain. Core Russian interj meaning 'oh' in everyday speech.
Often with annoyance. Core Russian adv meaning 'again' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (root 'винуть'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to office'.

examples.text: Мне в кабинете надо диван подвинуть.
examples.trans: I need to move the couch in the office.

examples.text: Привет, Вика, тебе снова нужно помочь?
examples.trans: Hi, Vika, do you need help again?

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach
meanings.note: К + dative. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come up (to), to approach', paired with 'подходить'.
Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come up (to), to approach', paired with 'подходить'.

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: по порядку = in order; всё в порядке = everything is fine

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.note: Informal: family and friends. Core Russian interj meaning 'hi' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'appeared in a dream'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и присниться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and appeared in a dream on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют присниться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to appeared in a dream.

examples.text: А я думала, мне это приснилось!
examples.trans: And I thought I dreamed that!

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'permission, permit' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня есть официальное разрешение на снос.
examples.trans: I have official permission for demolition.

examples.text: Кто посмел принять тебя без моего разрешения?
examples.trans: Who dared hire you without my permission?

meanings.note: + dative of the person. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'решить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to allow, to permit', paired with 'разрешать'.
polite formula, at a door or before asking something

examples.trans: May we come in? Good day, sir.

meanings.note: Plural: дети. Common masculine noun meaning 'child' in everyday Russian.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

examples.trans: We were dancing. First they were rude and insulting over there.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: grammatically feminine even for a male dog

examples.text: Я гуляю с собакой в парке.
examples.trans: I'm walking the dog in the park.

examples.text: Простите, это собака дочери. Я с ней гуляю пока.
examples.trans: Sorry, it's my daughter's dog. I'm walking her for now.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to agree', paired with 'соглашаться'.

examples.trans: Admit it / Don't you agree, that's much better.

examples.text: Это гораздо лучше, чем двенадцать лет. Согласитесь?
examples.trans: That's much better than twelve years. Don't you agree?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.en: to go and come back, to pop over
meanings.note: 'Сходите!' = Go on, go and see. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (somewhere and come back)', paired with 'ходить'.

examples.trans: Yes, go on. Don't mix it up with another one!

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.
